query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a thin Ni interlayer on W surfaces prior to spark-plasma sintering will form a graded Ni–W–Cu interphase that reduces interfacial void formation under thermal and irradiation service and increases the composite’s thermal conductivity by over 10% relative to an untreated W–Cu composite.
generation.material_initial_state: W–Cu composite comprising interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix, produced by SPS at 900 °C, 50 MPa, 10⁻³ Torr, without any interfacial coating.
generation.intervention: Deposition of a ~100 nm Ni coating on all W surfaces before sintering.
generation.conditions: Sintering: SPS at 900 °C, 50 MPa, 10⁻³ Torr, 30 min; service: 800 °C under 1 dpa neutron irradiation in He coolant.
generation.structural_mediator: Ni–W–Cu intermetallic interphase at the W/Cu boundary.
generation.mechanism: Ni interlayer promotes wetting and interdiffusion, forming a graded solid solution that lowers interfacial energy, suppresses void nucleation under thermal stress and irradiation, and enhances thermal contact conductance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Post-irradiation thermal conductivity >10% higher and interfacial void density >20% lower than untreated composite.
generation.baseline: Identical W–Cu composite made and tested without Ni coating.
generation.boundary: Valid for SPS processing at 850–950 °C, 30–70 MPa, hold times ≈30 min, and service conditions up to 1 dpa irradiation and 900 °C in He coolant; untested beyond these limits.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; performance gain may vary with Ni thickness and exact sintering parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of W–Cu composites (with and without 100 nm Ni on W) by SPS under identical conditions. Expose both to 800 °C, 1 dpa neutron irradiation in He. After irradiation, measure thermal conductivity by laser-flash and quantify interfacial void density via SEM image analysis.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if Ni-coated samples do not show at least 5% higher thermal conductivity and at least 20% lower interfacial void density than untreated controls.
